# Persistence Results for Chemical Reaction Networks with Time-Dependent Kinetics and No Global Conservation Laws

Authors: David Angeli, Patrick De Leenheer, and Eduardo D. SontagAuthors Info & Affiliations

https://doi.org/10.1137/090779401

## Abstract

New checkable criteria for persistence of chemical reaction networks are proposed, which extend and complement existing ones. The new results allow the consideration of reaction rates which are time-varying, thus incorporating the effects of external signals, and also relax the assumption of existence of global conservation laws, thus allowing for inflows (production) and outflows (degradation). For time-invariant networks, parameter-dependent conditions for persistence of certain classes of networks are provided. As an illustration, two networks arising in the systems biology literature are analyzed, namely a hypoxia network and an apoptosis network.

# Persistence in delayed chemical reaction network systems with time-varying kinetics

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.sysconle.2025.106206Get rights and content

## Abstract

Persistence is one of the most theoretically and practically important properties in the chemical reaction network theory. In the present paper, we give a sufficient condition for delayed chemical reaction network systems with time-varying kinetics to be persistent, that is, any positive solution to the non-autonomous delay differential equation (DDE) describing the time evolution of concentrations of species in the system does not approach the boundary of the positive orthant. In order to prove this, we first define the \omega $\omega $-limit set, and reveal some basic properties of it. On the basis of them, we characterize the intersection of the \omega $\omega $-limit set and the boundary, where the invariance cannot be defined in contrast to the autonomous case. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
